//: This file controls when Claude Code asks for your permission before running a command or
editing a file, and when it just goes ahead. It has three lists:
allow - Things Claude Code will do WITHOUT asking. Reserved for routine, low-risk,
reversible actions (installing packages, running project scripts, git commands
that don't destroy history, read-only file/folder inspection, deleting throwaway
ask   - Things Claude Code will always pause and ask you about first, even in modes that
would otherwise auto-approve. Used for commands that can permanently discard work
(deleting files outside scripts/, resetting or discarding git changes).
deny  - Things Claude Code is never allowed to do, no matter what. Used to protect secrets
(.env files, which often hold passwords/API keys) and to keep it out of core
'defaultMode: acceptEdits' means file edits are auto-accepted by default; the allow/ask/deny
lists below still apply on top of that for specific commands.
See https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/settings for the full permission syntax.
